To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

light-induced phosphorylation of ROS rhodopsin leads to a decrease in the permeability of the ROS disk to Ca2+ and that this decrease is due to the phosphorylation of a protein in the disk membrane which is distinct from rhodopsin.

(a) the Ca2+ permeability of isolated ROS disks is regulated in the dark by the level of rhodopsins phosphorylation, and that (b) the Ca2+-dependent release of Ca2+ from the ROS is also regulated in this way.

the permeability of the disks to Ca2+ is increased in the presence of light and MgATP, that the light-dependent increase is abolished by the addition of a phosphatase, and that the increase in Ca2+ permeability is correlated with the light-dependent phosphorylation of rhodopsins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of light and rhodsopsin phosphorylation on the permeability of ROS disks to Ca2+.
the permeability of ROS to Ca2+ and the effect of light on this permeability.
the effect of bleaching rhodopsin and rhodopsiin phosphorylation on the permeability of ROS disks to Ca2+.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of light and rhodoopsin phosphorylation is to regulate the permeability of ROS to Ca2+.
the phosphorylated form of rhodopsins is more permeable to calcium than the non-phosphorylated form, but only if the ROS are incubated in light.

the phosphorylation of rhodopsins in the ROS is not a necessary step in the process of bleaching, but that it is a step which may be important in the control of the permeability of ROS to Ca2+ and which may be involved in the regulation of the responsiveness of the rod outer segment to light.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phosphorylated rhodopsin has a reduced ability to bind to the Ca2+-binding protein, calmodulin.

light causes the permeability of the ROS disk membrane to Ca2+ to increase, that this permeability is regulated by rhodopsin kinase, and that the effect of rhodopsins’ phosphorylation is to decrease the permeability of ROS to Ca2+.
light and rhodpsin phosphorylation are involved in the regulation of the Ca2+ permeability of ROS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rhodopsin kinase is a Ca2+-activated protein kinase.
rhodopsin kinase is a Ca2+-dependent kinase and that the phosphorylation reaction is inhibited in the presence of Ca2+ ions at concentrations which are known to be present in ROS (10−7 M)1,3.
rhodopsin kinase is a Ca2+-activated enzyme, and that its activity is regulated by Ca2+ influx into the ROS.
